questions.question: State the two purposes of graphics in Technology and explain, with an example, why words alone cannot replace a drawing.
questions.expected_answer: Graphics develop ideas, because drawing a design reveals undecided details and lets ideas be tested cheaply on paper, and they communicate ideas, so that a product can be made by someone other than the designer. Words alone fail because they cannot convey shape, proportion, position and size at once: a paragraph describing a pair of pliers would not let a friend make a matching pair, whereas a dimensioned drawing following the conventions would let a carpenter in another city build a desk exactly.

questions.question: Describe the four line types used in Technology drawings and explain how scale and dimensions are shown.
questions.expected_answer: Outlines, the visible edges, are dark continuous lines; construction lines, the setting-out guides, are feint; hidden detail, edges behind a surface, are dashed; centre lines are a chain of long and short dashes. Scale is written on the drawing and states the ratio of drawn size to real size, for example 1 to 2 for half size. Dimensions give the real sizes in millimetres without writing the unit, each on a thin dimension line with arrowheads and extension lines, written once above the line where clearest.

questions.question: Explain the purpose of free-hand sketching and give four points of good technique.
questions.expected_answer: Free-hand sketching captures and compares ideas quickly, without instruments, while still being clear enough to communicate. Technique: hold the pencil loosely and further from the point; draw long lines in one confident stroke and leave a wrong line rather than rubbing it out; block in the shape with feint construction lines first and darken the outlines once proportions are right; use squared paper for straightness and proportion; and label parts with short notes and arrows.
